title: The Bone Market
text: Stalls of yellow bone under lanterns made from skulls, their candles burning in the eye sockets. The merchants have no faces, yet you can tell they are smiling. Every price here is fair, they say. Most of the prices are written in the buyer.

options.label: Pay in kind, and let the merchant choose whose flesh settles the price.

outcomes.text: The merchant takes its due with a little silver knife, gently, then gives good weight in return. The wound never quite stops aching.

options.label: Pay in honest gold, and keep your bodies your own.

outcomes.text: They take the coin with a sigh, as if you had refused a gift. Your purchase comes wrapped in cloth that smells of the grave.

options.label: Only look, and keep your hands to yourselves. Nothing here is free to touch.

outcomes.text: One stall sells nothing but the sound of your own names. You hear them whispered all the way out of the market.
Watching the faceless haggle, you learn their one rule: never speak first.
You linger too long at one stall. Slowly, every faceless head in the market turns toward you.
